agent_notes: Several first-choice URLs 404/403 (Seriously Fish oto/ancistrus, Aquarium Co-Op turbo/bristlenose, Tankflare, Hepper); used other pages. Quotes taken from WebFetch extraction output. No page states an amount of supplement per grazer except frequencies; no page states that feeding lets you keep more grazers (lifts mostly not-stated).

sources.states: 2-3 turbo snails per 20-30 gallons
sources.quote: 2-3 turbo snails are recommended per 20–30 gallons

density.note: Worldwide Corals (1 per 10 gal) appeared only in a search snippet; not citable.

sources.states: overstocking leads to lack of algae and starvation
sources.quote: Overstocking turbo snails can lead to a lack of algae, which causes starvation.

sources.states: too many grazers exhaust natural algae
sources.quote: don't overstock a small system—too many grazers quickly exhaust natural algae.

sources.states: supplement with dried seaweed when algae is insufficient; no amount
sources.quote: If algae levels are insufficient, supplement the diet of the Turbo Snail with dried seaweed.

sources.states: nori sheets or algae wafers if roaming without food; no frequency
sources.quote: if they keep roaming without finding food, supplement with nori sheets or algae wafers to prevent starvation.

supplement.note: No amount or frequency on opened pages.

sources.states: multiple grazers need enough algae; supplement if keeping multiple
sources.quote: Yes, but only if the tank has enough algae to support multiple heavy grazers.

lifts.note: Ties count to algae supply; no number of extra snails.

sources.states: 1 snail per 5 gallons
sources.quote: For this reason it is wise to stock no more than one snail for every 5 gallons of aquarium water.

sources.states: 1 per 10 gallons
sources.quote: One nerite per 10 gallons is a reasonable stocking guideline

sources.states: 1-2 per 10 gallons
sources.quote: One or two nerites per ten gallons provides effective glass and hardscape cleaning

sources.states: can starve if not enough algae
sources.quote: nerite snails can starve to death if there is not enough algae in the tank

sources.states: new clean tank gives little to eat
sources.quote: A brand-new, spotlessly clean tank won't give them much to eat

sources.states: supplement a few times per week when algae scarce
sources.quote: you should supplement with blanched vegetables or algae wafers a few times per week

sources.states: algae wafers, blanched zucchini, canned green beans; no amount
sources.quote: offer them algae wafers, blanched zucchini slices, and canned green beans to graze on

supplement.note: Frequency only; no quantity per feeding.

lifts.note: No opened page states a higher count with feeding.

suggest.note: 1 per US gal as general rule

sources.states: 1 per gallon
sources.quote: As a general rule of thumb, you can keep one Malaysian Trumpet Snail per gallon of water.

density.note: Species breeds without a male and tracks food, so a fixed density is weak.

starves.note: No opened page says trumpet snails starve.

sources.states: commercial food or vegetables 2-3 times a week
sources.quote: If you choose to feed your snails commercial food or vegetables, two to three times a week should suffice.

sources.states: algae wafers and pellets; no amount
sources.quote: You can supplement their natural diet with things like algae wafers and pellets.

sources.states: overpopulation when too much food available
sources.quote: Oftentimes, overpopulation will occur if there are too many food sources available.

lifts.note: Population rises with food supply; no number.

suggest.note: 3-6 in 20 US gal; 4-6 per 10 gal on another page

sources.states: 3-6 in 20 gallons
sources.quote: Three to six otocinclus in a 20-gallon tank represents a comfortable stocking.

sources.states: min 10 gal for 4-6
sources.quote: Otocinclus need a minimum of 10 gallons for a group of four to six

sources.states: best in mature tank with algae and biofilm
sources.quote: they do best in a mature aquarium with lots of algae and biofilm

sources.states: clean tank starves
sources.quote: If your tank is clean and sterile, they will starve.

sources.states: stable-tank algae not enough for 6+
sources.quote: algae build up in a stable aquarium usually won't be enough to completely sustain 6 or more Otocinclus

suggest.freq: daily (Aquarium Breeder); blanched veg 3x weekly (Furry Critter)

sources.states: daily algae wafers and blanched veg
sources.quote: Feed them daily with algae wafers and blanched vegetables.

sources.states: blanched veg three times weekly
sources.quote: If you're supplementing with vegetables, three times weekly is adequate.

lifts.note: No page says feeding permits more fish.

sources.states: 20 gal minimum for one adult; no per-volume ratio
sources.quote: A 20-gallon aquarium is a common minimum for one adult bristlenose pleco.

density.note: Tank minimum only, not a density.

sources.states: aquarium algae does not give a complete diet
sources.quote: They graze on algae, biofilm, and plant matter, but aquarium algae usually doesn't provide a complete diet.

suggest.freq: wafers every other day; refresh vegetables every 8-24 h

sources.states: algae wafers every other day
sources.quote: Algae wafers can be fed to your fish every other day.

sources.states: replace vegetables every 8-24 hours
sources.quote: Replenishing your fish's vegetables every 8-24 hours will keep them from rotting and making your fish unwell.

sources.states: offer wafers, vegetable pellets, blanched veg if food runs low
sources.quote: If their food sources in the tank seem to be running low, you can offer them some of the following:

sources.states: min 30 gal, 55+ long term; no per-gallon ratio
sources.quote: need a minimum of 30 gallons, with 55 or more appropriate for long-term housing.

sources.states: should not rely exclusively on aquarium algae
sources.quote: Algae wafers are highly recommended because Siamese Algae Eaters should not rely exclusively on aquarium algae.

suggest.food: algae wafers, blanched vegetables, sinking pellets

sources.states: supplemental foods daily even when algae available
sources.quote: Siamese Algae Eaters should receive supplemental foods daily even when algae is available.

sources.states: diet must be supplemented with veg
sources.quote: As detailed below, the diet must be supplemented with other foods including a good vegetable component.

lifts.note: Furry Critter says well-fed adults reduce algae consumption, the opposite of a lift.

sources.states: 1 Amano per 2 gallons
sources.quote: As a good rule of thumb, you can add 1 Amano Shrimp per 2 Gallons.

sources.states: 10 gal minimum then 2 gal per extra shrimp
sources.quote: After that, you’ll want to add two gallons for every additional shrimp in the tank.

sources.states: less likely to survive in pristine tank without algae
sources.quote: Your shrimp are less likely to survive if you put them in a pristine tank without any algae.

starves.note: Fishkeeping World also says shrimp always need supplementing (quote only matched as a label, dropped).

sources.states: core diet pellet or algae wafer
sources.quote: The core of their diet should consist of a high-quality pellet or algae wafer.

sources.states: blanch vegetables, remove after 1 hour
sources.quote: Remove the veggies from your tank after one hour to avoid contaminating the water.

sources.states: more algae/debris means less supplementing needed
sources.quote: Obviously the more amounts of algae and debris in the tank for them to graze on, the less supplementing they will need.
